title: Add newly-required constructor parameter and forward to base (CS7036)
problemSignature: CS7036: There is no argument given that corresponds to the required parameter '<name>' of '<CoreType>'

requiredRepoCharacteristics: client subclass overrides a Core base constructor

exclusions: Do not invent the parameter type. Read the required parameter from the decompiled installed DLL signature (or, if the exact target commit of a local read-only Core reference repo is known/pinned, git show/git grep against that commit is acceptable equivalent-or-better evidence -- confirmed workable in a full multi-minor-version run, cbmi 7.6.3->9.2.1).
Do not change the client override body.

Also check whether an EXISTING parameter's type changed (e.g. plain interface -> Lazy<T>) rather than assuming every CS7036/CS1503 pair is purely a new-parameter-count problem -- confirmed to occur at least once (EntityService, partnerExpenditureReportingExportExcelService wrapped in Lazy<> between 7.6.3 and 9.2.1).

Also check whether an existing constructor parameter was already being captured locally (e.g. into a private field) but simply never forwarded to base() -- fixing this can be as simple as adding the existing identifier to the base(...) argument list, no new parameter needed (confirmed for FundingIdeaService.userRepository and PaymentService.coreAppSettings).
rootCauseHypothesis: Core added a required constructor dependency (or changed an existing parameter's type); the client subclass constructor and its base() call must forward the new/changed parameter.
proposedActions: Decompile the Core base type to read the new constructor signature (or read source directly from a pinned local reference-repo commit if available).
Diff param-by-param against the client's existing derived constructor and base() call -- do not assume only additions; also check for type changes on existing params.
Add the matching parameter to the client subclass constructor (or reuse an existing uncaptured/unforwarded one).
Forward it in the base(...) call in Core's exact required order/name.
Register the new dependency in DI if it is not already registered.

Rebuild and confirm the CS7036 family reaches zero -- expect cascading discovery: fixing one non-compiling file can reveal new CS7036 errors in previously-blocked downstream files on the next build; this is not a regression.
successfulEvidence: memory/episodes/ep-cbmi-core9x-001.json (11 applications across a 7.6.3->9.2.1 multi-minor jump: EntityRepository, EntityService, FinancialActualService, FundingIdeaService, IdeaService, PartnerExpenditureReportingService, PaymentService, ProjectService, StakeholderService, SendGridMailService, IdeasController)
